Subject: Reserved GPU capacity: tactical architecture review and prep

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. To get the engineering review scheduled (pool sizing, autoscaling behavior, and isolation patterns), can we lock a 60–75 minute deep-dive next week? The goal: align on your peak concurrency profile, confirm isolation requirements (tenant-level vs. workload-level), and walk a tentative runbook for autoscale thresholds and fallback policies.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Mon 2027-05-10 10:00–11:15 (preferred)
- Tue 2027-05-11 08:00–09:15
- Tue 2027-05-11 11:00–12:15

Attaching a one-page agenda and a short playbook draft so you know what we plan to cover. If you have a specific SLO/throughput matrix or sample traces, please drop them in the Drive link below before the session.

Preliminary agenda (attached):
- 10 min: objectives & success criteria
- 20 min: workload profile review (throughput, seq len, hot paths)
- 20 min: pool topology & isolation tradeoffs
- 15 min: autoscale policies, warm pools, burst paths
- 10 min: open items & actions

Attaches: agenda-draft.md
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X_example_capacity_docs

If none of the slots work, tell me your timezone and two windows that do and we’ll adapt.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@orbital.ai>

Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 12:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU capacity: tactical architecture review and prep

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear agenda. The Mon 10:00 PT slot works for me and I can pull in our infra lead (procurement@orbital.ai will forward to the right person). A couple of asks before we meet:
- Can you add a short slide/section on our options for strict data isolation (we're evaluating tenant-level VPC isolation vs. software namespacing for PCI scope).
- We need to confirm whether warm pool sizing can guarantee X ms cold-start tail for synchronous inference — if you have historical numbers for 8k token-ish workloads, that would be helpful.

We'd like the session recorded for our internal review.

Regards,
Jordan

Jordan —

Confirmed for Mon 2027-05-10 10:00–11:15 PT (calendar invite sent: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=reserved-gpu-review-20270510). We'll record and share the transcript.

Quick notes on the asks:
- Isolation: we'll bring a short comparison slide that covers tenant-level VPC routing + dedicated pools vs. process/namespace isolation inside a shared pool, including tradeoffs for network controls and auditability.
- Warm pool tail: historical median and p95 numbers depend heavily on model size and quantization; Marcus will bring a couple of measured examples for 7B and 70B-equivalent setups (8k token window). We'll also note how prefix caching and batching affect tail latency.

Attachments included for prep: capacity-playbook-v1.pdf (short checklist + sizing templates). Please review the sizing worksheet in the Drive folder earlier if you have current p95 latency targets; we'll use that to propose pool counts and warm sizes.

Action owners for the session:
- Marissa: run through Orbital workloads and success criteria (you)
- Marcus: autoscale policy patterns & observed tail-latency slides
- Neha: isolation + compliance notes, PCI considerations
- Karthik: runbook and fallback options, SLA language

See you Monday.

—Karthik
